chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Fifty weeks of theaters and traveling by Pullman
summary: Until Christmas 1935 the band played long theater tours, travelling in a private Pullman and baggage car so they avoided Southern hotels, sometimes coupled to Duke's train.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So then I played -- I stayed with Cab up until 19 -- well, say Christmas of 1935. And we used to play 50 weeks of theaters, right straight across the board from New York to California every year. And then -- well, I'll say 40 weeks
and then we'd come into the Cotton Club for a couple months and go right back out on the road again.
Then we traveled by Pullman, you know. Like when we went down South where you couldn't get any hotels or anything, we always traveled by Pullman.
So you didn't have to go through all that?
No, they'd put us in -- like we had a special baggage car and special Pullman car.
Did they put you on a siding (in-audible).

Put us in on a siding, go play the job, come back to the train and go to sleep and wake up in the next town. And it was beautiful in there. Sometimes we'd have Cab's train, coaches, and Duke's hooked onto the same train because they'd be going to the same --
